title: Killing preserved under agreement on fixed variables
statement: Let $t$ be a term on $n$ variables and let $\rho, \sigma : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Option}\,\mathrm{Bool}$ be two restrictions such that $\sigma(v) = \rho(v)$ for every variable $v$ that $\rho$ fixes (that is, whenever $\rho(v) \neq \mathrm{none}$). If $t$ is killed by $\rho$, then $t$ is also killed by $\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: t is a term on n variables
ρ and σ are restrictions on n variables
σ agrees with ρ on every variable ρ fixes (ρ v ≠ none → σ v = ρ v)
replaced:
If a term $t$ is killed by $\rho$ and a restriction $\sigma$ agrees with $\rho$ on every
non-free variable (i.e.\ $\sigma(v) = \rho(v)$ whenever $\rho(v) \neq \mathrm{none}$), then
$t$ is also killed by $\sigma$.
